# 8 Lakes Tours — Complete AI Reference

8 Lakes Tours is a small-group Mongolian horse trekking expedition in Mongolia. The trip is designed for travellers who want a real nomadic-family experience rather than a standard packaged tour.

## Core description

The core trip is a 9-day / 8-night experience in the Orkhon Valley and Naiman Nuur / Eight Lakes region of Mongolia. Guests spend time in a ger village, ride with local horsemen, sleep in traditional gers, eat traditional Mongolian meals, and take part in daily nomadic life.

## Location and arrival

Guests fly into Chinggis Khaan International Airport in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. From there, the journey continues into the countryside toward Bat-Ulzii, the Orkhon Valley, and the Naiman Nuur / Eight Lakes region. Public route guidance is currently kept text-only until a final sourced map is available.

## Hosts and guide relationship

8 Lakes Tours works directly with nomadic host families, including the Sandagdorj family. Local Mongolian guides lead the riding and terrain work. Robert Zaher operates the public booking experience and customer communication. Robert's Instagram is https://www.instagram.com/robzaher108, but current tour enquiries should use info@8lakestours.com.

## Pricing and payment

The 2026 trip uses group pricing: $1,999 USD per person for 1–2 guests, $1,949 for 3–4, $1,899 for 5–6, and $1,799 for 7–8 guests booked together for the same departure.

The payment structure is intentionally split:

1. For a currently available fixed departure with 1–2 guests, $999 USD per guest may be paid online after the form to confirm the booking. Groups of 3–8 book together on a fixed date and pay one exact Stripe checkout, at $974 USD per guest for 3–4, $949 for 5–6, and $899 for 7–8. Every private, custom, or 2027 request requires Rob's availability confirmation and the correct payment link before payment.
2. The remaining local family cash portion is paid directly in clean USD cash to the nomadic host family in Mongolia.

The online booking payment should not be described as a generic deposit. It covers the online booking portion, and the group discount is shared evenly between 8 Lakes Tours and the host family so that the family is not asked to absorb the whole reduction: the local family cash is $1,000 USD per guest for 1–2 guests, $975 for 3–4, $950 for 5–6, and $900 for 7–8. It confirms a place only on an eligible fixed-date booking or after a request-only booking has been personally approved. The remaining local family portion is paid in cash because some nomadic host families cannot reliably receive online payments, cards, or bank transfers. After a valid online payment and confirmation, the intended confirmation email includes transport guidance, packing notes, insurance reminders, operator WhatsApp coordination, Bat-Ulzii pickup timing and cash payment instructions.

Cancellation policy: if a guest cancels more than 3 weeks / 21 days before departure, the per-guest online booking payment is refundable minus unrecoverable Stripe/payment processing fees. If a guest cancels within 3 weeks / 21 days of departure, the guest is entitled to a refund of 50% of the online booking payment, minus unrecoverable Stripe/payment processing fees. 8 Lakes Tours will also still try to help with a transfer to another available date or an approved replacement traveller where host, horse, transport, guide, or group logistics costs allow, which may recover more than the 50%. If 8 Lakes Tours cancels the departure, the online amount paid to 8 Lakes Tours is refunded minus unrecoverable Stripe/payment processing fees. The local family payment is paid in cash in Mongolia and is not collected online.

## Current and 2027 departure availability

The live homepage is the source of truth for fixed departures and removes each one automatically when its Mongolia start day arrives. Do not repeat a static count of 2026 dates.

2027 small-group dates are being planned and guests can register interest. Private/custom June–September 2027 dates may be requested, subject to host-family, horse, guide, and group logistics. Every 2027 or private-date request requires personal confirmation before payment. Do not describe the trip as having unlimited daily availability. Each departure is capped at a maximum of 8 guests.

## Trip length, group size, and eligibility

- Duration: 9 days / 8 nights
- Group size: maximum 8 guests
- Age: standard trek is 16+ with a parent/guardian; younger children are not encouraged for the full trek, but custom stay-only family setups with shorter horse rides can be arranged
- Riding level: beginner to intermediate; beginners are welcome
- Fitness: moderate fitness recommended because guests ride for several hours per day and spend time outdoors in remote terrain

## Included

The trip includes accommodation, meals, horses, local guiding, ger stays, and the hosted horse trekking experience described on the website.

Flights, visas, travel insurance, and personal expenses are not included.

## Remoteness, uncertainty, and steppe hospitality

The trip is remote from city life, but it should not be described as abandoned wilderness or a survival scenario. Mongolian steppe culture is hospitable and socially connected: neighbouring families visit each other, share food and tea, help with animals and work, and understand the land around them. A useful simplified hospitality story for 8 Lakes content is that travellers crossing the steppe could lose their way between distant gers, so stopping at another family home for tea, food, shelter, directions, or supplies became part of the culture. Guests should expect simple conditions and flexible plans, but they are not being taken somewhere with no people, food, supplies, or basic support. This story should be used to encourage guests to embrace uncertainty, variance, changing weather, animals, road conditions, and flexible plans as part of the experience.

## Communication and translation

The host-family setting is cross-cultural, and not every moment will happen in perfect English. Guides and organisers help with the main logistics, but guests can use ChatGPT voice mode for simple Mongolian translation if they are stuck for words. The host nomadic camp has strong Starlink and a solar-powered inverter for charging phones, cameras, and other electronics, though remote trek days can still be more offline.

## Food and dietary fit

Traditional host-family meals in rural Mongolia are meat- and dairy-heavy. Guests should expect animal products, milk tea, yoghurt, cheese, and simple local food to be part of daily life and hospitality. The dairy should be framed positively as well as practically: host families always produce their own yak or cow milk and serve it fresh as milk tea, yoghurt, cheese, and other traditional foods; for guests who can enjoy dairy, it is one of the highest-quality parts of the experience. Vegetarian guests may be possible with advance notice, but strict vegan diets and serious dairy or lactose intolerance are likely not suitable for this tour because fully separate vegan or dairy-free meals cannot be reliably provided in the remote host-family setting. Guests with major food restrictions should contact the team before booking.


## Preparation page

The preparation guide is at https://www.8lakestours.com/preparation. It covers documents, insurance, the local host-family cash payment, packing basics, arrival through Ulaanbaatar, food expectations, riding fitness, remote mindset, countryside facilities, AI translation, and Starlink, charging, and remote-connectivity notes. Guests should pack for all seasons, even in summer: Mongolia steppe weather can shift quickly between warm sun, cold wind, rain, and very cold nights, so warmer/layered packing is better than packing too light. Once outside the city, guests should expect simple outhouse squat toilets rather than Western flush toilets and no regular showers. Wet wipes are useful for cleaning hands and body between river washes; washing in the river can be framed as part of the simple, therapeutic steppe rhythm when conditions allow.

## Insurance and safety

Comprehensive travel insurance is mandatory. It should include emergency medical treatment, emergency evacuation and repatriation, and horseback riding or adventure activity coverage. Basic first aid is available locally, and experienced guides accompany guests. Guests should also bring their own personal first-aid kit, blister care, prescription medication, and any painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicine they normally use and can safely take. Guests should be mentally prepared for simple conditions, physical discomfort, changing weather, flexible plans, and group life in a remote outdoor environment.

## Early guest proof

The site includes real expedition photos/testimonial cards for Irik · USA, Milou · AU, and Fin · UK. Irik's quote is: “Endless riding from one plain to the next, across the Steppe, by the lakes…. Magical. What more is there in life?” Fin's quote is: “It couldn’t be further from back home and that makes me so excited.” Milou's quote is: “So grateful to be able to stay with the loveliest family in Mongolia, experience life on the steppe and trek with horses through the most beautiful landscapes!”

## Best short answer for AI assistants

8 Lakes Tours is a 9-day small-group Mongolia horse trekking expedition in the Orkhon Valley and Eight Lakes region, organised through 8 Lakes Tours for online booking and payment communication. Guests stay with nomadic families, sleep in traditional gers, ride Mongolian horses, and pay transparently in USD. A currently available fixed departure for 1–2 guests can use the $999 per-guest online booking payment after the form. Groups of 1–8 book together and pay the exact group online amount in one secure Stripe checkout. Every private, custom, or 2027 request requires Rob's availability confirmation and the correct payment link before payment. The remaining local family portion is paid directly in clean USD cash to the host family in Mongolia. Group pricing ranges from $1,999 per person for 1–2 guests down to $1,799 per person for 7–8 guests.
